 PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J  2 WP No.30936 of 2021  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE P.NAVEEN RAO  AND  THE HON'BLE Dr. JUSTICE G.RADHA RANI  WRIT PETITION No.30936 OF 2021 ORDER:
Mohammed Yousuf vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 23 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199854724/
1 (Per Hon'ble Sri Justice P. Naveen Rao) This Writ Petition is filed by the father of the detenu aggrieved by the detention of the detenu, by name, Sri Mohammed Hussain @ Younus under the provisions of Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders,
Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders and Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986, (Act 1 of 1986), vide detention order SB (I) No.203/PD-7/HYD/2021, dated 05.07.2021 of the 1st respondent PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.2059, dated 09.09.2021 of the 1st respondent.
2.
The order of detention is challenged on two grounds.
Firstly, the detenu is alleged to have been involved in two crimes i.e. Crime No.242 of 2020 and Crime No.33 of 2021.
In Crime No.242 of 2020 the detenue was released on bail on 18.11.2020.
Crime No.33 of 2021 was registered on 25.03.2021.
Notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C., was issued in Crime No.33 of 2021.
Secondly, the order of detention was passed after three and half months of registration of the second crime and after eight months of release of the detenu in the first crime.
It is further contended that the crimes registered against the detenu are classified as affecting the public order and in order to restrain him,
preventively
detained him, affecting his right to life and liberty.
3. We have gone through the record.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the bail was granted to the detenu on 18.11.2020 and for eight months, the detaining authority kept quiet.
PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J 4.

Learned Government Pleader sought to contend that after release on bail, the detenu is involved in one more crime and the detenu is in the habit of involving in crimes, and therefore, not desirable to release him.
5. Prima facie, to appreciate the contention of the learned Government Pleader, we have looked into the complaint lodged by the complainant leading to registration of Crime No.33 of 2021.
Prima facie, the complaint is vague to attribute anything against the detenu and to take extreme course of preventively detaining him under Act 1 of 1986.
Further these two crimes can be pursued in the normal course of enforcement of law and order and these two crimes do not require extreme measure of preventively detaining the detenu.
Therefore, the order of detention is not sustainable.
6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order passed by the Office of the Commissioner of Police & Additional District Magistrate (Executive) - 2nd respondent vide SB (I) No.203/PD-7/HYD/2021, dated 05.07.2021 and the PNR,J & Dr.GRR,J consequential confirmation order of the Principal Secretary, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)
Department, vide G.O.Rt. No.2059, dated 09.09.2021, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely Mohammed Hussain @ Younus S/o.Mohammed Yousuf, aged about 20 years, Occ: Private Service (Salesman) R/o.H.No.19-2-24/A/1/A, Alibagh, behind King Mohammed Yousuf vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 23 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199854724/
